subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own an Agentic OS-specific lease-backed session-spawn protocol and its SQLite recovery state, or should this remain in the downstream integration behind a generic core extension seam?
rationale: The repository policy explicitly reserves optional service workflows and owner-specific behavior for plugins, ClawHub, or owner repositories when current seams suffice; deciding whether a new generic core seam is warranted is product and API ownership judgment, not a mechanical patch choice.

options.title: Keep the contract owner-side
options.body: Move the Agentic OS protocol, state, and docs to the downstream integration and use existing supported Gateway/plugin seams where possible.

options.title: Sponsor a generic core seam
options.body: Approve a narrowly named owner-neutral lease or spawn-authorization extension API, then require the downstream integration to implement its own protocol on top of it.

options.title: Accept the core contract
options.body: Explicitly accept Agentic OS as a permanent public core Gateway and persistence contract, with full API and upgrade ownership.

recommendation.title: Keep the contract owner-side
recommendation.body: Move the Agentic OS protocol, state, and docs to the downstream integration and use existing supported Gateway/plugin seams where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: A core Gateway API, SQLite state, and integration-boundary decision needs repository-level product ownership.
